bill.title: Public Safety First Act
bill.latestActionText: Read twice and referred to the Committee on the Judiciary.
bill.officialSummary: Public Safety First Act This bill requires the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) to detain certain non-U.S. nationals ( aliens under federal law) who have been arrested for burglary, theft, larceny, or shoplifting. Specifically, DHS must detain an individual who (1) is unlawfully present in the United States or did not possess the necessary documents when applying for admission; and (2) has been charged with, arrested for, convicted of, or admits to having committed acts that constitute the essential elements of burglary, theft, larceny, or shoplifting.

classification.plainSummary: This bill would require the Department of Homeland Security to detain individuals who are in the United States without authorization or proper documentation and who have been charged with, arrested for, convicted of, or admit to committing burglary, theft, larceny, or shoplifting. The bill mandates detention for this specific category of individuals rather than leaving detention decisions to agency discretion.

industries.rationale: Mandatory detention requirements would increase demand for immigration legal services and representation in detention proceedings.
The bill would impose new operational requirements on DHS detention facilities and immigration enforcement agencies.

plain.whatItDoes: This bill would require Homeland Security to detain certain people who are not U.S. citizens ( aliens under federal law) who have been arrested for burglary, theft, larceny, or shoplifting.
plain.whoItTouches: People applying to live here, and their families here.
plain.everydayEffect: If it passed, the change would show up in an application, and how long it takes. Nothing has changed yet. Most bills never become law.
plain.source: Reworded from the official summary. Staff at the Congressional Research Service wrote that summary. It is public domain, and the full text of it is further down this page.

method.formula: score = Σ_industries ( donorShare(industry) × billWeight(industry) ), where billWeight = classifierConfidence / Σ classifierConfidence. Range 0–1, read as a weighted share of disclosed itemized money.

ordinary.text: They wrote this bill. Sponsoring a bill about your own district's industry is the ordinary case, not the odd one.
Lawyers & Lobbyists is also the top donor sector for 2 other members from TX. That points to the industry being big in the state, not to anything about this member.

disclaimer: This tool places two public records next to each other: who donated to a member of Congress, and what that member legislated on. Any overlap you see is a correlation, not causation. It is not evidence of a quid pro quo, of influence, or of wrongdoing. Legislators routinely receive support from industries in their district for the same reason they legislate on them: those industries are there.
